title: Detailed latency telemetry and dashboards by endpoint & model (streaming vs non-streaming)
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a set of telemetry and Grafana dashboards that surface latency distributions by model and API route, with clear splits for streaming vs non-streaming flows. Current console views show aggregate latency across models and traffic types which hides regressions in specific model-route combinations. This work will add per-route, per-model percentiles (p50/p95/p99), histogram and heatmap visualizations, and an explicit streaming vs non-streaming breakdown so SREs and product engineers can quickly identify regressions and capacity issues. Instrumentation changes include tracing hooks for request lifecycle attribution and pipeline changes to ensure metrics and logs join correctly to model and route tags.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards show p50/p95/p99 latency for each public API route and each served model variant (by model_id and version)
Streaming and non-streaming requests are split into separate series/panels with consistent percentiles and raw percent distribution histograms
Each dashboard panel supports model and route filters and time-range selection aligned with existing console UX
Trace links from a dashboard panel open to the tracing UI with span attribution to the model shard and runtime node
Metric emission does not increase cardinality beyond agreed tagging scheme and passes cost review
Automated tests that validate metric names/tags are present in CI and a load test verifies percentile stability under synthetic traffic
implementation_plan: Finalize tagging schema: route, model_id, model_version, streaming=true|false, route_version
Add tracing hook at request routing layer to attach model and route tags to root span
Emit latency metrics at two points: end-to-end request and model-generation-only (token loop), with consistent tags
Update metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> OpenTelemetry collector -> long-term storage) to ensure route and model tags persist
Create Grafana dashboard templates with panels for percentiles, histograms, heatmaps, and cohort comparisons
Instrument additional logs to include model_id and request_id to support join-based debugging
Run canary load and synthetic scenarios to validate percentiles and validate no large tag cardinality spikes
Ship dashboards behind a feature flag and iterate on queries with PM and SRE feedback
dashboards_panels: Overview: Time-series p50/p95/p99 for all traffic with model and route selector
Model-Route matrix: heatmap where x=route, y=model, cell=p95 latency
Streaming vs Non-streaming split: side-by-side percentiles and histograms
Latency histogram: bucketed distribution for selected model+route
Trace jump: quick links from high-latency cell to top traces in tracing UI
Regression detector: sparklines with anomaly markers for model-route combos
instrumentation_changes: Add model_id and model_version labels at the request router level
Attach streaming=true/false flag to request context and to emitted metrics
Expose token-loop timing separate metric to isolate model compute latency
Ensure tracestate/span tags include shard_id and runtime_node_id for downstream correlation
Limit non-essential dynamic labels (e.g., dataset names) to control cardinality
tracing_hooks: Hook A: RouterEntry - create root span and add tags: route, route_version, user_tier
Hook B: ModelDispatch - add child span with model_id, model_version, quantization_profile
Hook C: StreamChunk - add events for each stream frame with sequence index
Hook D: CacheHit - span annotation when KV cache is hit/miss for a request
log_pipeline_changes: Add structured fields to request logs: request_id, model_id, route, streaming
Ensure log ingestion pipeline preserves model and route fields for log-based metrics
Create a join view linking logs to traces by request_id in ELK/Kusto
Add sampling rules: full traces for errors and tail-latency requests, sampled traces for nominal traffic
alerts_and_slo: Create temporary alert: model-route p95 > 2x baseline for 5m
Define SLO targets per-class: hosted-critical routes p99 < 1.2s, non-critical p95 < 2.5s
Add alert when tag cardinality increases >15% relative to baseline
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for metric emission and tag schema in the metrics lib
Integration test: synthetic replay that asserts p50/p95/p99 in dashboards match expected ranges
Load test: 10k rps synthetic mix to validate histogram stability and no schema explosion
Observability QA: PM and SRE run adopted checklist and approve dashboard queries
rollout_plan: Feature-flag dashboards + instrumentation in staging for 48h
Monitor tag cardinality and metric volume; roll back if cost exceeds threshold
Gradual rollout to 10% production traffic, monitor for 72h
Full rollout and public console exposure after sign-off from SRE and PM
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Tag cardinality growth increases cost - Mitigation: enforce allowed tag values and caps, preflight cardinality estimate
Risk: Tracing overhead impacts latency - Mitigation: sample traces, avoid heavy serialization on hot path
Risk: Dashboards mis-attributing streaming requests - Mitigation: add dedicated streaming flag and end-to-end tests
Risk: Query performance in Grafana for large cardinality - Mitigation: precompute aggregates and use rollup tables
